name: Nuclear risk
value: No US–Russia treaty limits since 5 Feb
summary: No US–Russia strategic arms limits since New START lapsed on 5 Feb; Zaporizhzhia worker killed by drone on 9 Nov
state: New START expired on 5 Feb with no replacement, and the US did not answer Russia's offer to keep its central limits for a year (Arms Control Association). The IAEA said a drone killed a worker at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant on 9 Nov, and its head called the strikes unacceptable (The Moscow Times). Searches on 13 Nov found no nuclear test, change in alert levels or explicit threat of nuclear use, so the level stays at Watch.
for_you: There is no change in official UK guidance. The main risks are an arms-control gap and safety at Ukraine's occupied nuclear plant, which the IAEA monitors on site.
rubric_hit: Watch: arms-control lapse without replacement (New START expired 5 Feb); no test or alert change

sources.title: Arms Control Association — New START at a glance
The Moscow Times — Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant worker killed in drone attack, IAEA says

why: Nuclear use anywhere would be a civilisational shock; arms-control treaties are weaker than at any time since the 1960s.
drivers: Threats in active wars, testing, doctrine changes, arms-control collapse, proliferation.

rubric.alert: A nuclear test, changes in deployment/alert levels, or threatened use in an active conflict.
rubric.watch: Explicit threats, unusual exercises, doctrine changes, or arms-control lapses without replacement.
rubric.normal: No explicit nuclear threats or tests; arms-control dialogue active.
